av_event.line_text: Gemma: I just mean, put your numbers in front of them. Don't wait for them to notice. They won't.
av_event.what: A brown-and-white cocker spaniel walks into the bottom right of Gemma's frame, picks the tennis ball out of the grey dog bed in its mouth and trots back out of shot, while Gemma keeps talking and doesn't look round.

text:
B: Alright. Darren.
A: Hi. Gemma. You're Basingstoke, aren't you? Callum said.
B: Brighton Hill. You?
A: Chineham. What do you do?
B: Branch manager. Builders' merchant on the estate out past the ring road.
A: Which one?
B: The one by the tip.
A: Oh, I know it. My husband's an electrician, Craig, self-employed. He's probably been in.
B: Probably. Most of them come in for something. Moaning, usually.
A: That sounds like Craig.
B: Ha. You're cars, Callum said.
A: New cars, franchise on the retail park. I'm top of the board this month.
B: Right. Good for you.
A: Do you have targets?
B: Head office figures. Stock, margin, shrinkage. Quarterly review's coming up, so they'll be picking it apart. I'm going for area manager, so it matters a bit more this time.
A: Oh, same. Well, sales manager. If they don't give it me in a couple of years I'll move.
B: My problem's the meetings. Half the people who get promoted are just good at talking in meetings. I'd rather get the job done, to be honest.
A: You need both, though, yeah? If nobody upstairs knows you're getting it done, it doesn't count.
B: Maybe. Not sure I agree, but go on.
A: I just mean, put your numbers in front of them. Don't wait for them to notice. They won't.
B: Yeah. Fair enough, I suppose.
A: What do you drive?
B: Er, company van in the week. I've got a car on finance. Needs its MOT booking, I keep forgetting.
A: When it's up for renewal, come and see me. I'll sort you out.
B: That's what Callum said. Not sure I trust either of you.
A: You shouldn't trust Callum. You can trust me.
B: Ha. Right. What d'you do weekends, then?
A: Gym, three times a week. Weights, rowing. You?
B: Same, three mornings. Weights. Knee's gone for running.
A: I did the Basingstoke Half last year. Two hours four.
B: Kelly drags me to parkrun. I'm at the back. Erm, yeah, so... Friday curry?
A: Indian or Nando's. Craig decides.
B: Chicken madras. Every week.
A: Every week? You don't fancy something else?
B: No. Why would I?
